**Merge keeps the history, rebase rewrites it.**

Merge ties the two branches together with one new commit. Both lines of work stay visible forever.

Rebase copies your commits onto the tip of the other branch. You get a straight line, but they are new commits with new IDs.

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph After merge
    m1[main] --> mc[merge commit]
    y1[your work] --> mc
  end
  subgraph After rebase
    m2[main] --> y2[your work, recopied]
  end
```

**When to reach for each**
- Rebase your own branch onto fresh `main` before you share it. Reviewers get a clean, readable line.
- Merge when landing finished work into `main`. The merge commit records when the branch arrived.
- Never rebase commits someone else has already pulled. Their copy and yours stop matching.
